---
title: "Use proj from R"
subtitle: "Preview an analysis, find its files and build its outputs from R."
---

The projcli R package calls the standalone proj command. Keep working in R while
using the same project paths and build workflow as the command line. It is a
separate package from the existing projr package.

[Function reference](r-reference.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}
[Configuration](configuration.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary}

## Availability

| Component | Status |
|---|---|
| R package projcli 0.0.0.9000 | Available in frontends/r/projcli in this repository; not on CRAN. |
| M4 R helpers and complete CLI queries/session controls | Included in published preview.5 and merged source. |
| Optional R setup/maintenance below | Included in published preview.5 and merged source. |
| Published command download | [Preview.5](install.qmd); installing the R package does not replace it. |

Use preview.5 or a matching newer source command for the supported API. Preview.4
can support basic calls, but does not include the complete R queries/session controls. Errors
do not silently trigger an engine switch or binary download.

## Installation

Requirements: R 4.1 or newer, processx 3.8 or newer, jsonlite 1.8 or newer, and a
separately installed proj command. The package does not embed Rust. There is no
CRAN install.packages("projcli") release.

Install the ordinary dependencies deliberately in an R console:

~~~r
install.packages(c("processx", "jsonlite"))
~~~

Download the [preview.5 source archive](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/archive/refs/tags/v0.4.0-preview.5.tar.gz),
set the R working folder to its root, then install the R subdirectory:

~~~r
install.packages("frontends/r/projcli", repos = NULL, type = "source")
library(projcli)
help(package = "projcli")
~~~

This does not install proj, renv or analysis dependencies. The [CLI install guide](install.qmd)
covers the released binary and its limits. Use the published preview.5 command for these features. Building the command from
source is optional and needs Rust/Cargo, as described in the repository README.

proj can also name unrelated software. You can select an exact command:

~~~r
options(projcli.binary = "/absolute/path/to/proj")
proj_cli("capabilities")
~~~

Selection checks an explicit binary argument, that option, PROJCLI_BIN, then PATH.
Analysis children do not inherit interactive R options. For the example below,
put the intended command on PATH so parent and child R processes find it.

## Quick start

This example creates and removes its own temporary project. The selected CLI and
R package must be available to its R analysis child.

<!-- R_QUICKSTART_BEGIN -->
~~~r
library(projcli)

project <- tempfile("proj-r-example-")
dir.create(project)
writeLines(c(
  "directories:",
  "  cache: {path: _tmp}",
  "  output: {path: _output}",
  "build:",
  "  scripts: [analysis.R]",
  "  git: false"
), file.path(project, "_proj.yml"))
writeLines(c(
  "out <- projcli::projr_path_get('output', 'results.csv', format = 'absolute')",
  "dir.create(dirname(out), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)",
  "write.csv(data.frame(value = 42), out, row.names = FALSE)"
), file.path(project, "analysis.R"))
projr_version_set("0.1.0.1", only_if_exists = FALSE, project = project)

projr_build_dev(project = project, execution_dir = "project")
preview_file <- projr_path_get(
  "output", "results.csv", project = project, format = "absolute")
stopifnot(read.csv(preview_file)$value == 42)

projr_build_patch(
  msg = "Example build", project = project, execution_dir = "project")
final_file <- projr_path_get(
  "output", "results.csv", project = project, safe = FALSE, format = "absolute")
stopifnot(read.csv(final_file)$value == 42)
read.csv(final_file)

unlink(project, recursive = TRUE)
~~~
<!-- R_QUICKSTART_END -->

Expected: one value,42. The preview keeps the project version and does not publish
final outputs. The patch build promotes successful output. Git is disabled and no
upload target is configured in this example. Paths are explicit; lookup itself
does not create directories. Your analysis still controls its own writes.

## Read settings and parameters

These helpers use the CLI's typed query commands:

~~~r
settings <- projr_yml_get(project = ".")
seed <- projr_par_get("model", "seed", project = ".")
~~~

Keys are literal names. Missing parameters return NULL. Requested configuration
values can include secrets; avoid publishing them. See the
[configuration functions](r-reference.qmd#configuration).

## Optional R setup and maintenance

The CLI provides explicit setup commands:

~~~r
proj_cli("init", c("readme", "--rmd"))
proj_cli("init", "renv")
~~~

README.Rmd is created without replacing plain README.md. The renv command uses
already installed renv to set up an empty project and initial lockfile; it refuses
existing renv state or .Rprofile. Setup does not enable build actions.

Choose production tasks independently:

~~~yaml
build:
  r:
    document: true
    readme: true
    renv-snapshot: true
~~~

They default off. document uses installed devtools to generate documentation;
readme uses rmarkdown to render README.Rmd to README.md; renv-snapshot records
dependencies before start hooks and again before post-build documentation/README.
It does not restore packages. Install optional task dependencies deliberately.

In the merged preview.6 source, VERSION remains authoritative and the named build/version
helpers synchronize an existing DESCRIPTION by default. Set
settings.sync-description-version: false to leave DESCRIPTION unchanged. An explicit
legacy backend retains its original version policy. Citation support is separate.
[Exact task reference](configuration.qmd#optional-r-project-setup-and-build-maintenance-local-candidate)
covers prerequisites, order and bounded recovery.

## Restore packages explicitly

For a trusted project with renv.lock and already installed renv:

~~~r
dir.create("restored-library", showWarnings = FALSE)
receipt <- proj_renv_restore(".", "restored-library")
receipt$packages
~~~

This restores locked versions in an existing project-contained library. It does
not install renv, update the lockfile, activate your interactive session or run
automatically during builds. Installation can execute package code and affect its
cache. See the [dependency reference](r-reference.qmd#dependencies).

## Keep an explicit legacy backend

~~~r
projr_build_patch(backend = projr::projr_build_patch)
~~~

That existing function runs in your R session with its original arguments, results
and effects; the old package must already be installed. No automatic fallback occurs.
Bookdown render_book, legacy DESCRIPTION authority, arbitrary renderer objects, dev bump/
cache deletion, implicit path creation and caller-state hooks are outside the
supported CLI-wrapper subset.

Plain analysis R processes are isolated by default. config.r.session: shared
reuses a child for plain scripts in a build, not your interactive process. Hooks
and renderers remain separate; config.r.rscript selects an installed executable.
[Execution reference](configuration.qmd#r-processes-and-executable) covers libraries,
working folders and startup behavior. The maintenance post batch is separate;
there is no permanent background daemon.

## Evidence and limits

The named M4 gate compared unchanged Weisberger01+04 scripts and complete CSVs
between clean projr and the new engine on matched R4.6.1, with report checks, local
archive, fresh data/dependency restore, rerun and deliberate failures.
[Integrated evidence](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/actions/runs/40268103232)
does not establish whole-paper/historical-runtime reproduction, CRAN acceptance or
full legacy parity. The existing projr package is unchanged.

Browse the [function index](r-reference.qmd) or use help(package="projcli") locally.

## Explicit init options in preview.6 source

The [project setup reference](cli/init.qmd) covers purpose/contact questions,
--description-file, --readme-rmd, --renv and --citation. Use the existing
proj_cli("init", args, project = ...) transport for those exact options. The named R helpers below adapt those same CLI actions. R package scaffolding and automatic
citation-author inference are not implied.


## R initialization helpers

The merged preview.6 source adds projr_init, projr_init_plan, projr_init_readme,
projr_init_license and projr_init_renv. They use the shared CLI, with explicit R
metadata values. Only opted-in renv setup checks its optional suggested package;
installation requires interactive consent or explicit install_missing=TRUE.
See the [named R reference](r-reference.qmd#initialization) for examples, defaults and library details.
